source.title: Simply B1 Preliminary for Schools: 8 Complete Practice Tests (2019, revised exam from 2020)
source.answerKeyOrigin: Prepared for WordHop from the supplied reading text; not a publisher-provided answer key.
source.explanationOrigin: Written for WordHop with evidence from the supplied text.

questions.explanation: Entrants must be under eighteen, so adults cannot enter. The story must be about magical people and places rather than a true personal event.
questions.evidence: You must be under 18 years old to enter.

questions.explanation: The advertisement requires gardening work on two named days each week throughout the summer. It asks applicants to telephone, not email.
questions.evidence: Your services will be needed twice a week, on Tuesdays and Fridays.

questions.explanation: Peter says he lent Andrew the geography book and now urgently needs it for a test. This means Andrew borrowed it from Peter.
questions.evidence: Do you still have the geography book I lent you last week?

questions.explanation: Trains are passing the flooded station without stopping, so passengers cannot get off there. Staff are already working on the problem.
questions.evidence: Trains will not be stopping at the next station today.

questions.explanation: John's mother asks him to buy several items while he is in town. Blue-top milk is her first choice; green-top is only the alternative.
questions.evidence: When you go to town today can you get me a few things?

questions.explanation: Super Extra fits three travellers, has a sea-view window and a large wardrobe, and includes the fridge's drinks and snacks in the price. No balcony is required.
questions.evidence: all the drinks and snacks in the fridge are included in the price

questions.explanation: Deluxe Super has two bedrooms, a large balcony and meals delivered to the cabin. These features match the family's wish for an especially luxurious cruise.
questions.evidence: The Deluxe Super includes meals in your cabin.

questions.explanation: The Standard cabin is the cheapest option and is intended for people who mainly sleep in their cabin. Donna does not need a window or extra facilities.
questions.evidence: This is great for people who want to save money and only sleep in the cabin.

questions.explanation: Deluxe has separate bedrooms and a living room. Unlike Deluxe Super, its description does not include meals served in the cabin.
questions.evidence: two bedrooms, a bathroom and a living room

questions.explanation: The Suite has two separate bedrooms with double beds, balcony access from each room and a fridge of drinks and snacks. This matches both travellers' requirements.
questions.evidence: The Suite cabin has two separate bedrooms both with double beds.

questions.explanation: Paula's mother found the newspaper advert and showed it to her. Paula applied online, but that is not where she first heard about the vacancy.
questions.evidence: my mum gave me the local newspaper and showed me an advert for the local zoo

questions.explanation: The manager phoned after Paula returned home from the interview. Therefore, he told her she had the job on the same day they met.
questions.evidence: when I got home, I got a phone call from him saying that I got the job

questions.explanation: Paula reached the zoo before opening time and found the gates locked. The manager arrived later at nine o'clock.
questions.evidence: I was there too early and the gates were still locked.

questions.explanation: The manager supplied a uniform to wear over Paula's normal clothes and a pair of boots. She did not replace her own clothes or immediately clean the lion's cage.
questions.evidence: gave me a uniform which I had to put on over my normal clothes

questions.explanation: Paula had difficulty finding a vacancy but eventually found a weekend job she loves. She would encourage a friend to keep looking for something suitable.
questions.evidence: each week I am taken to work with other animals and people. I really love it!

questions.explanation: The previous sentence introduces the family trapped above the bakery. C explains how they escaped when the stairs were blocked.
questions.evidence: There was a family living above the bakery who couldn't get out down the stairs.

questions.explanation: The houses were almost touching, so fire could spread easily between them. F gives that consequence before the writer introduces the dry weather and strong wind as further problems.
questions.evidence: the houses were also built very close together

questions.explanation: A describes the general effort to fight the fire. The following sentence uses 'Even the king' to add a particularly surprising example of someone helping.
questions.evidence: Even the king came out to help the firemen.

questions.explanation: 'This' refers to destroying buildings to make a gap. E explains that the action slowed the fire, although it did not stop it immediately.
questions.evidence: the firemen destroyed many buildings to create a big gap

questions.explanation: H introduces the paragraph's account of effects that the passage presents as beneficial, following the description of destruction and homelessness.
questions.evidence: Architects helped to rebuild London and built wider streets so a new fire couldn't move quickly.

questions.explanation: 'Available to the public' means ordinary people could access or use it. This fits the opening of internet access beyond its earlier users.
questions.evidence: it wasn't until the 1990s when it became (21) ... to the public

questions.explanation: A bank can 'offer' a service such as online banking. The other choices do not fit the normal verb used for providing this service.
questions.evidence: the first bank in the world to (22) ... online internet banking

questions.explanation: 'Dial-up connection' is the expression for internet access made through a telephone line.
questions.evidence: The computer needed to use a telephone line.

questions.explanation: The computer sent signals through the telephone line. 'Signals' fits communication; signs and the other options do not describe these transmissions.
questions.evidence: sent noisy (24) ... like a fax machine does

questions.explanation: 'Make or receive phone calls' is the normal pair of expressions for outgoing and incoming calls.
questions.evidence: you couldn't make or (25) ... phone calls

questions.explanation: A network connects devices to one another. The sentence lists the different devices linked by the internet.
questions.evidence: computers, satellites, mobile devices and other gadgets in a network

questions.explanation: 'Ones' replaces the plural noun 'services' to avoid repeating it. The repeated noun 'services' is also grammatically possible.
questions.evidence: There are many types of emergency services, but the three main (27) ...

questions.explanation: 'Have to' expresses what a caller must do. 'Need to' is another correct way to give the same instruction before 'dial'.
questions.evidence: you (28) ... to dial 999 and tell the operator what service you want

questions.explanation: '24 hours a day' means continuously throughout each day. It is paired with '7 days a week'.
questions.evidence: All the emergency services operate 24 (29) ... a day, 7 days a week.

questions.explanation: The previous sentence gives an eight-minute target. 'Not' explains that reaching a remote location in that time is sometimes impossible.
questions.evidence: especially if the situation is in the middle of the countryside, far from the city

questions.explanation: 'Each' refers separately to every emergency service and agrees with singular 'service has'. 'Every' also fits this meaning and grammar.
questions.evidence: (31) ... emergency service has their own special vehicles

questions.explanation: The phrase 'drive through red lights' means continue past a red traffic signal rather than stop at it, as emergency drivers may need to do.
questions.evidence: This includes driving (32) ... red lights.
